newsitem.title: USA: Centurion sets OK Mine copper plant funds.
newsitem.headline: Centurion sets OK Mine copper plant funds.

text.p: Centurion Mines Corp said Wednesday an agreement to sell $7.5 million of convertible debentures will provide the funding needed for a copper plant at the OK Mine near Milford, Utah.
Centurion said it anticipates copper production will begin in the last quarter of 1997, with no additional financing required thereafter.

Pointing out this will mark its change to a production company from an exploration company, Centurion said it expects net profits in excess of $4 million per year at present copper prices after operations begin.
The company said it has an investment banker that has agreed to manage placement of 13.5 percent debentures.
Centurion said it will use the proceeds to construct and operate a solvent-extraction electrowinning copper recovery plant at the 100 percent owned mine.
The company said it has identified a copper oxide resource in excess of 80 million pounds of recoverable copper.

A preliminary production feasibility study by an outside mining consultant firm concluded the OK Mine is economically viable and estimated costs at $0.60 per pound of copper produced. Mine life is expected to be a minimum of 10 years.

Mine and plant permitting is well advanced and no permitting delays are expected, Centurian said. Various right of way, and ground water usage permits have already been issued. Utah State air quality, ground water discharge, and reclamation permits are in the final review stage and are expected by March.
